text.p01: To everyone who has ever felt unseen: may a friend always bend down to listen. A story about empathy and seeing through a friend's eyes.
text.p03: On the wide golden plain lived Langa, the tallest young giraffe of all. From way up high, he could see hills and the rising sun.
text.p04: Every morning he raced to the waterhole to meet his friends. Clomp, clomp, clomp! went his big hooves. "Good morning, everyone!"
text.p05: Down by his hooves, Themba the meerkat sneezed. Langa's running had kicked up a big cloud of dust, right under his little grass hat.
text.p06: "Achoo!" But Langa didn't hear. His head was way up in the breeze. "What a beautiful day!" he called. "Everything looks fine from up here!"
text.p07: At lunchtime, Langa nibbled the sweetest pods from the very top of the acacia tree. Down below, the little animals looked up, tummies rumbling.
text.p08: "Why don't you just stretch?" Langa asked kindly. Themba stretched on his tiptoes. The tortoise stretched his neck. But the pods stayed far, far away.
text.p09: In the afternoon they played Follow-theLeader. Clomp, clomp, clomp! Langa took giant steps over the bushes. Nobody else could keep up.
text.p10: Langa looked down at all the droopy faces. "Why is everyone so grumpy?" Themba sighed. "You can't see it from up there."
text.p11: That night, under a big round moon, Langa found Themba by the old baobab. Bending down felt wobbly and silly. But Langa wanted to know.
text.p12: He spread his front legs wide, wider, WIDEST, and lowered his long neck all the way down to Themba. "Show me," he said.
text.p13: Next morning, Themba led him into the grass. Down low, it was a tall, tickly forest. When warthogs trotted by, dust puffed into Langa's eyes.
text.p14: "Now you know how it feels," said Themba gently. Langa blinked. His own big hooves had been making dust clouds every single day.
text.p15: Langa stayed down low and listened. The tortoise said the bank was too steep to reach the water. The guinea-fowl chicks said grass hid everything.
text.p16: And everyone said the sweetest pods grew much too high. Langa felt it deep inside, right under his heart-shaped spot. "I never knew," he whispered.
text.p17: So Langa got busy. He pressed his big hooves into the muddy bank, making little steps, one, two, three, down to the water.
text.p18: He bent the acacia branches gently down. And now he walked softly, clomp... clomp... clomp... so no dust puffed into anyone's eyes.
text.p19: One evening, everyone gathered on the hill to watch the sun go down. Langa noticed Themba at the very back, standing on his tiptoes.
text.p20: Themba wasn't saying a word. But Langa knew that feeling now. He bent his long neck down low. "Climb up," he said. "Come and see."
text.p21: Themba climbed up Langa's long neck and stood between his two little horns. The sky glowed pink and purple, all the way to the hills.
text.p22: "So this is what you see!" Themba gasped. Langa smiled. "And now," he said softly, "I can see what you see, too."
text.p23: From that day on, Langa looked down as often as he looked up. Whenever a friend went quiet, he bent his neck low to listen.
text.p24: After the first rain, the plain turned green. Clomp... clomp... went Langa's gentle steps. When we truly see each other, we all grow taller. The End
text.cover: The View From Down Low. A Story About Empathy and Seeing Through a Friend's Eyes
